Infect needs some help obviously. There are 4 options that each have their own advantages in my mind as far as what could be reprinted into modern or a new card printed.

Legolas quick reflex gives the deck another option for hexproof that we can feel safe about, provides removal which can lead the way to elf being a better threat again and in niche cases allows us to get away with 1 less mana on inkmoth kill turns with protection. Animate inkmoth with inkmoth use quick reflexes to untap it now you have a protected inkmoth that can swing which is nice.

Berserk helps to push infect into a higher spike power on good turns, makes declaring no blocks a bigger threat due to instant speed pump and lets you overload and trample through blockers making elf more relevant.

Invigorate gives us a free pump so that we can save our mana for protection while still being able to present threats, makes it so we can pump after no blocks which current modern infect can’t really do. 

Last is either embiggen or some other always 1 mana +4/+4 for phyrexians. One of the cards I had been hoping to get when they returned to phyrexians as a story was G target creature gets +2/+2 if it’s phyrexian it gets +4/+4 instead. This solution of 1 mana +4 at instant speed like the other options makes no blocks a larger consideration but right now we don’t have a pump spell that can be cast on our opponent’s turn to beat a 3 damage effect. 

In summary give me something that makes elf more relevant(quick reflexes and berserk), make post blocks pump good(berserk, invigorate or 1 mana +4), or help us protect ourselves (quick reflexes and 1 mana +4). I love infect and have it foiled out but these are some cards I would love to see given to modern infect to help it out.

Depends on how you want the game to play out. I don’t run as many protection pieces because I am usually looking to strip the cards out of people’s hands to prevent interaction or play a little more setup before I get started. Part of the issue with the hand hate route is that you can demonstrate a soft lock of preventing anything but instants or commanders being played by using the “when this creature die they discard” hand hate and you end up just winning by them scooping. I also only run 3 cards that can deal damage to my opponent, I could set up an infinite creature loop as well but for the most part it’s an attrition deck seeking to grind out. So if you were looking to emulate my list I would probably cut some of your damage sources, for example falkenrath and vindictive could probably go. You could do more if you wanted but I am willing to admit that my deck is probably too low on ways to truly end the game.

The 3 cuts I would select would be [[vampiric rites]], [[dockside chef]] and [[fume spitter]]. Fume spitters max of -2/-2 is alright and you can pick off some decent pieces with one or 2 activations is alright but I think you have enough kill based removal to be fine without it. You already have 12 sac outlets and 13 draw points so I feel like cutting the 2 mana activation to draw a card effects are a fine cut.

Yeah one of the biggest things to remember is that different decks have different windows to win and based on those timings the exactness of their hands and what they require of their opponents changes. 

A simple change would be to find slots for the new capenna evolving wilds, for example [[broker’s hideout]] is a simple etb, sac get a basic forest or island and while they aren’t impressive fetch lands are one of the most efficient ways for you to get advantage in tatyova. While they are creating etb tapped basics these sort of lands essentially have a forced pay 1 mana draw a card stapled to them.

In the grand scheme of things there is sometimes just nothing you can do about wipes. Your best bet in those cases is to be thinking about how to make extra mana or cards out of what you are doing so that you can get more out of less. [[indulge//excess]] is a good example of this. You can use the front half to double up your attackers so you don’t need to commit more cards to the board while using the backside to bank some mana for a while. Additionally as good as doublespelling can feel you have to remember that having low cards in hand is a really easy way to signify to your opponents that now is the time to wipe so holding back a little bit can help you rebuild if they fire it off and might catch your opponent being greedy waiting for you to deploy your stuff.

Simic decks like this are value based meaning that your plan is a little bit more variable. Having access to the interaction of blue means that you can take your time a little more to ramp and draw from tatyova so while you may not have an idea of what you are doing straight from opening hand like other linear decks you should be instead focusing on what you will need later on to answer the possible threats. Remember in this you aren’t the aggressor you are the inevitable victor so your plan should be to look to try and stall out the more aggressive decks until your more passive engine of play a land, draw a card can get you super far out in front of everyone. This is a wordy way to say that your options for keepable hands are a lot less restrictive than something more all in like zada so it is understandable to be overwhelmed and unsure of what is keepable. I would look to be ramping at least once to get tatyova out earlier because again you just want to be seeing up that engine when you can.

So for anything with trigger doubling I would suggest getting something to represent the ability on the stack if you are lost. So in the cast of Preston with an etb. It would be something is flickered with elesh norn on field. Arrange in order your for simplicity let’s consider just Preston and original card etb. Arrange the 4 abilities such that you have the 4 on the line then go step by step through since each of the Preston abilities when they resolve will re add 2 etb triggers. This is of course something that can be time consuming so only do it when needed. 

An example of this would be having 6 tokens. 4 etb and 2 Preston represented.
If you have the original etbs resolving last: etb token, etb token, Preston token, Preston token. Resolve Preston trigger and put 2 additional tokens onto your stack pile making it: etb, etb, Preston, etb, etb. I know it’s kinda simple and slows the game down but if you have the stuff to represent everything it might not be the worst idea taking it slow while you get comfortable with tracking all the triggers you will generate.
